display.title: Ner Mitzvah: Your Neshamah Is a Little Menorah
display.summary_short: Chanukah is over, but its light stays: the neshamah is Hashem's candle, mitzvos are the candle and Torah the flame, and we must share that light with others.
display.summary_long: A talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, given right after Chanukah. Uncle Yossi explains that when we lit the menorah we also lit our own little menorah, the neshamah, which the verse calls Hashem's candle. It gives light through Torah and mitzvos: a mitzvah is like the candle and the Torah like its flame, and neither gives light alone. So, as the Sages teach, learning is not enough; what counts is putting it into action. Living this way brings peace, health, long life and true joy into the home, just as the Chanukah lights did. Like the menorah, which spreads its light in every direction, a soldier of Tzivos Hashem must not keep things to himself but share what he knows about Hashem, Torah and mitzvos with relatives and friends, making them bright lights too. In this merit we pray to see the great light of Moshiach and the golden menorah in the Beis HaMikdash.
display.lesson: Keep your neshamah lit by putting Torah into action, and share your light with others.
